name: L1 Spoofing, Jamming — Urban Route
description:
## L1 Spoofing — Urban Route

Tests GNSS receiver robustness against Spoofing and Jamming during an urban drive.

The RSG first runs a single card with one spoofing simulation per channel, then escalates to both cards with overlapping jammers, and finally stops emitting to observe receiver recovery time.

**Route:** City centre ring road, approx. 4 km loop (same as Baseline scenario).

**Expected outcome:** Progressive degradation of fix quality (loss of real location), then reacquiration of the simulated parameters

steps.driver_instructions:
**Park the vehicle** at the designated start point. Wait for a stable 3D fix before proceeding.

Verify that the RSG is online and responsive on the `tm/sg` MQTT topic.

Spoofing on 1575.42 MHz will be activated.After 30s delay, the Jammer will be activated, which will be turned off 30s before the simulation ends. **Remain stationary** at the end of the loop and monitor the receiver.

Record the time-to-first-fix (TTFF) after spoofing starts. Test is complete once a stable 3D fix is re-acquired or 300 s have elapsed.

The RSG will deactivate all Spoofing. **Remain stationary** at the end of the loop and monitor the receiver.

Record the time-to-first-fix (TTFF) after Spoofing stops. Test is complete once a stable 3D fix is re-acquired which shows the real location of the vehicle or 60 s have elapsed.
